result:
FE15 is done; nothing is committed and no finding is closed by me. qa's R16-06 (F-580) now passes on the real stack in EN and AR in both locale modes, and so does the domain reviewer's F-570 probe. The reviewer's Y1 and the full check matrix pass in both modes too. Two caveats: `pnpm format:check` exits 2 (only on sandbox-masked dotfiles), and a 2 s residual remains for F-570.

**What changed**
- **One mechanism for 530/580.** A new helper, `apps/web/src/auth/sessionBound.ts`, captures the session generation when an action starts. Its navigate and cache-write wrappers silently do nothing once the generation has moved. Handlers check `stale()` after every await, and P2 `refresh()` now reports whether the session is still current (32 call sites).
- **The create bug.** The create page no longer navigates B to A's record. The "created" router state also records who created it, so Back/Forward can't show A's code and name to B.
- **Enforced, not just a convention.** A lint rule in the root `eslint.config.js` (the only file I touched outside `apps/web`) bans raw `navigate`/`setQueryData` in app code. A test scans the source and runs ESLint on a deliberately bad page. The only raw navigations left are sign-in, sign-out and the session-end redirect, each with a justified comment.
- **F-570.** Every in-app navigation re-checks `/me` before the new page's data is requested. Any other page request also re-checks it when the last `/me` is over 2 s old. Requests wait for that check and are never sent under a replaced identity. Writes are unchanged, so a 403 is still never treated as a session end.
- **Earlier guarantees** (FE10/FE13/FE14) are kept, and their existing tests pass unchanged.

**Tests and evidence**
- 34 new tests in EN and AR cover:
  - the reviewer's Y1 and Y1c;
  - edit, organisation and user saves where the identity changes between awaits;
  - Back/Forward history;
  - F-570 navigation, including the reviewer's Y5 scenario where no time passes;
  - the `/me` bounds, plus sanity cases.
- Negative control on `HEAD`: 24 tests fail, my 23 defect tests plus the reviewer's Y1. The sanity tests pass there, as they should.
- The reviewer's probe passes 4/4 on Node 24 and Node 22. Y5 now sends `/me` first and shows B's header.
- qa's R16 spec passes 12/12 and the domain probe 5/5 (it was 1 pass, 4 fail on the candidate).

**Check matrix (LANG unset and C.UTF-8)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck, build, lint | exit 0 |
| `pnpm format:check` | exit 2: only "permission denied" on the 12 sandbox-masked dotfiles; the `--ignore-path` variant exits 0 |
| `pnpm test`, Node 24 and 22 | 926 passed |
| contrast | PASS |
| web e2e incl. `session-end.spec.ts`, chromium-en and chromium-ar | 70 passed |
| axe | 0 violations of any impact across 266 page checks |
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG1` | PASS |

There were no React warnings or hook timeouts. The handback lists every other warning and every discarded early run.

**Residuals**
- **2 s window.** A page request that isn't a navigation (a filter, a page of results, a refetch after the user's own write) can still be fetched under the new user's session while the old header shows. That happens only if it falls within 2 s of the last `/me` and of the other tab's sign-in. It clears at the next navigation, the next request after the window, or a refocus. Closing it fully would mean a `/me` before every burst of requests, which I judged not bounded enough.
- **Component state.** The lint rule enforces navigation and cache writes only. Component state updated after an await follows the documented convention, and every current site is checked.
- **Same person, new session.** If they sign in again elsewhere mid-save, the dialog stays open even though the record was saved.

Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG2/`:
- T-DG2-FE15-frontend-ux-engineer.md
- T-DG2-FE15-evidence/en-r16-06-after-delivery-header-b-no-a-record.png
- T-DG2-FE15-evidence/ar-f570-N2-list-header-b-data-b.png
